subject: Urban Planning
title: The Grid: How Cities Got Electricity
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Grid: How Cities Got Electricity usable.

hook.text: In 1882, Edison lit up one square mile of lower Manhattan from Pearl Street Station — the world's first power grid.

buildup.text: Edison's system served 85 customers and powered 400 lamps. Within a decade, electric grids spread across every major city.

discovery.text: Tesla and Westinghouse won the 'War of Currents' with alternating current, which could travel long distances via transformers.

twist.text: The US grid is now 70 years old on average. Blackouts are increasing because aging infrastructure can't handle modern demand.

climax.text: Modernizing the US grid for renewable energy will cost $2.5 trillion. It's the largest infrastructure challenge of the century.

punchline.text: Edison lit a block. We need to rewire a continent. Same idea, bigger scale.

quiz.question: Why did alternating current win the 'War of Currents'?
options: It was safer for residential use than direct current
It could travel long distances efficiently using transformers
It was cheaper to generate at power stations
